title: kernel ringbuffer GPU OOM breadcrumbs (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: capture a reproducible breadcrumb trail for intermittent GPU OOMs seen on batch inference hosts (p4d-like). This is a messy running log — commands, snippets, hypotheses, things to try next.

Background/context:
- Hosts: rtx-a6000 and p4d-derived infra in staging. Occurs during long-running multi-tenant inference job (batched decoding).
- Symptoms: occasional sudden OOMs during token generation; sometimes followed by container crash, other times process stays up but subsequent CUDA allocs fail.
- Suspected contributors: kernel driver mismatch after driver update, memory fragmentation from persistent KV cache, CUDA/CUDNN ABI mismatch with packaged wheel, intermittent MIG partitioning artifacts.

Timeline of attempts and raw outputs:

2024-11-07 09:12 — initial repro run (local reproduce)
Command: docker run --rm --gpus all -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -v /models:/models redwood/serve:staging sh -c "python -u /app/run_batch.py --model /models/7b --batch 16 --max-tokens 512"
Output (truncated):
  ...
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/cuda/memory.py", line 80, in malloc
  raise RuntimeError('CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate %d GiB' % ... )
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 47.68 GiB total capacity; 39.35 GiB already allocated; 1.12 GiB free; 41.25 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

Notes: nvtop showed high reserved memory by PID 1234 (the runner). But `nvidia-smi` right before OOM reported 38GB used, which is close — not sure if fragmentation.

2024-11-07 09:20 — kernel ring buffer check (dmesg)
Command: sudo dmesg | tail -n 60
Output snippet:
  [123456.789012] NVRM: GPU 0000:3B:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [123456.789015] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3B:00): 79, pid 1234, 85e0c2f4e8c7cbf3
  [123456.789020] nvidia-modeset: Loading, GPU 0

Interpretation: Xid 79 often means a driver/kernel fault during a kernel launch (out of resources or illegal mem access). Could be caused by a driver mismatch.

2024-11-07 09:28 — check driver / toolkit versions inside container and host
Commands run:
  # in container
  python -c "import torch; import sys; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
  # container output: 1.12.0+cu116, '11.6', True
  # host
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version,name --format=csv
Host output: 525.85.12, 12.1, NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB

Mismatch observed: container expects CUDA 11.6 while host shows CUDA 12.1 (driver 525.x). Typically driver backwards compatibility allows older CUDA toolkit runtimes to work, but ABI mismatches between libcudart/libcuda could matter.

2024-11-07 10:05 — ldd on libtorch and libcuda inside container
Command: ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep cuda
Output: libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f4b)

Check host libcuda: ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 => symlink -> /usr/lib/nvidia-525/libcuda.so.1. OK.

2024-11-07 10:12 — tried forcing CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and limiting batch size
Commands tried: export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6,max_split_size_mb:128
and reduce batch from 16 to 8 -> less frequent OOMs but not eliminated.

2024-11-07 11:30 — reproduce with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get better stack traces
Command: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python -u /app/run_batch.py ...
Output (truncated):
  RuntimeError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
  /usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/cuda/_utils.py:xxx in _call_cuda
  torch._C._cuda_getDeviceProperties failed: unspecified launch failure

This pointed to an unsafe kernel launch, consistent with Xid 79.

2024-11-08 15:40 — journalctl check after container crash
Command: journalctl -k -n 200 | grep -i nvidia -A3 -B3
Output:
  Nov 08 15:37:12 host kernel: nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
  Nov 08 15:37:12 host kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: enabling device (0000 -> 0003)
  Nov 08 15:37:12 host kernel: NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (rm_init_adapter:1832)
  Nov 08 15:37:12 host kernel: NVRM: No kernel module is running for the NVIDIA graphics driver.

Guess: there was a transient driver module crash (maybe due to a kernel upgrade or out-of-tree module).

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Driver install drift: kernel modules were rebuilt or a driver upgrade happened on the host without draining/restarting nodes -> intermittent Xid 79s.
2) Memory fragmentation + large persistent tensors (KV cache) cause allocation failures that escalate to launch failures on subsequent kernels. Batching exacerbates fragmentation.
3) Python/pip wheel uses a mismatched libcudnn or cublas that tries to access newer driver symbols leading to an illegal kernel op (less likely but possible).
4) MIG/partition edge case: device being reconfigured mid-job -> driver sees device removed (falls off bus).

Notes on instrumenting next run:
- Enable nvprof/nvtx capture (if possible) for a small repro batch to pinpoint which kernel triggers Xid 79.
- Add periodic torch.cuda.memory_summary(device=0, abbreviated=True) dumps to logs every N steps to watch fragmentation over time.
- Capture /var/log/messages and dmesg to persistent log collector for postmortem; include kernel module list (lsmod | grep nvidia) at time of failure.
- Add CUDA mem hooks: set TORCH_USE_RTLD_GLOBAL=1? (experiment) and export LD_PRELOAD points to host libs to force using host-provided libcudnn.

Quick debugging commands to run on suspect host (one-offs):
- nvtop (interactive) or watch -n 0.5 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free,compute_mode --format=csv -l 0.5
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- for PID 1234: sudo ls -l /proc/1234/fd | wc -l; sudo lsof -p 1234 | grep nvidia
- pmap 1234 | tail -n 20 (check process virtual memory map)
- python snippet to dump torch.cuda.memory_stats() periodically

Things tried that didn't help (notes):
- Rebuilding driver to 525.85.12 on all hosts -> reduced frequency for a day but then recurred.
- Switching to a different torch build (1.12.1 vs 1.12.0) -> no change; still saw occasional Xid 79s.
- Turning off multi-threaded data loaders -> no effect (this is in inference path, not data loading).

Open action items (short):
- [ ] Re-run with instrumented small repro and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING + nvprof; capture kernel names. (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Add memory_summary logging to batch runner and push to centralized logs. (owner: Avery)
- [ ] Run host kernel/drivers audit across fleet and compare kernel module versions across nodes that experienced failures vs those that didn't. (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Create a minimal reproducer that allocs a large KV cache then does repeated small kernel launches to try to reproduce Xid 79. (owner: Maya)

Questions to ask infra/SRE:
- Were any kernel upgrades applied around 2024-11-06 through 2024-11-08 on the staging fleet?
- Any automated driver auto-updates enabled in the AMI or via image build that could cause module drift?

Scratchpad final notes (quick heuristics learned):
- Xid 79 + "GPU has fallen off the bus" usually indicates driver/module instability OR illegal kernel launch; correlate with dmesg/journal entries.
- PyTorch reserved bytes sometimes mask the true free memory; use memory_summary to see fragmentation stats.
- If the host driver reports CUDA 12.x while container runtime is built for 11.x, this is not automatic failure but increases chance for obscure ABI edge cases when third-party libraries (e.g., cuBLAS/cuDNN) are loaded from nonstandard paths.

If I get a clean repro I'll escalate to NVIDIA support with nvml traces and kernel logs.

-- end of scratchpad --
